title: Move money between gift cards without breaking a card's rules

blocks.text: The card service sells prepaid gift cards. By law a card holds at most `GiftCard.CAP` cents, and a card that has been cancelled (reported lost, say) takes no new money. `load` and `spend` already enforce this.
Customers now want to move money from one of their cards to another. Write `transferTo(target, cents)` in `src/main/java/practice/GiftCard.java`.

When you're done, money moved onto a card obeys the same rules as money loaded onto it, and a transfer that either card refuses throws `GiftCard.RefusedException` and leaves both balances exactly as they were. About three lines in total.

cases.says: a transfer between two open cards takes the amount off one and adds it to the other
a transfer larger than the sender's balance is refused and changes neither card
a transfer to a cancelled card is refused and the cancelled card's balance stays as it was
a transfer that would take the target card over the cap is refused, so every rule of the target applies, not only the ones the sender checks
when the target refuses, the sender keeps its whole balance

origin.section: Private Is Checked per Class, Not per Object

concepts: private is checked per class, not per object: code in a class can read and write the private fields of any instance of that class, so it bypasses that instance's own checks unless it goes through its methods.
